steps.text: Late night
Rhodes Island Landship, 'Just One More Pint' Bar

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Dario...

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Yes, ma'am?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Can I drink yet...?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Today, I—

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Yes, yes. You've told me plenty of times.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: You had to teach some kids who weren't listening, and you fought the reserve operators in a drill to test both their limits and yours, which led you and the other instructors into a heated, 'friendly' conversation.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Would you like me to repeat your ramblings?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Very well, then.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I just want some booze!

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Ten more minutes, ma'am. We serve alcohol after 9. Those are the rules.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Following all those rules will kill you one day!

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Following rules is what gives our lives order.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: If you are not happy with that, I am sure you know with whom you can file a complaint.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: We are just staff members here, and we must follow the rules she made.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Grr...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Gimme an apple juice.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Coming right up.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I worked my butt off the whole day, and I can't even get a sip of booze...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: If I were—
If you were younger, you would've flipped the table and put your electric blade to his throat.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hank?! What are you doing here?!

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I've been here the whole time, Instructor Makayla.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Don't use my real name here. I'm Dur-nar.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Instructor Dur-nar.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Drop the 'Instructor.'

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: That's a no-go, Instructor.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Ma'am, your drink.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Thanks...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: *Sigh*, everyone's so stubborn, you're all a bunch of burdenbeasts...

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Thank you for the compliment, Instructor.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Thank you for the compliment, ma'am.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: That wasn't a...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Whatever...

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Would you like something to drink, sir?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Ice water, please.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Coming right up.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hah... How come I've trained up a man like this...?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Takes a gulp of apple juice)

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Go on, Hank... What are you up to now?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I'm usually out in the field as a liaison between Blacksteel and Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Our partners at Blacksteel are here for a meeting, and I'm their bodyguard. I'll be taking them back once they're done.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Sounds like something you'd do.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Did anyone get hurt on your way here?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: We had some injuries, but nothing too serious.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: It's all thanks to your teaching, Instructor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: The stuff I taught you back then is way outdated by now. Keep using those tricks, and not even the Originium armor they're testing in the military can save you.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: They've already deployed that armor to a few teams.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Not the original either, mass produced ones, usually to elite soldiers like you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, count me out. I can't wear that stuff.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: You can. Even Big Mark wears it fine.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Finishes the apple juice)

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, you haven't changed one bit. Just a few sentences and you drive the conversation into a dead end.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Sorry, Instructor.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Here's your ice water.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Speaking of Big Mark, where is he?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: The guy wrote in for me, and got everyone to sign off on the paperwork to let me work here, but he's too busy to come see me?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Big Mark isn't a Rhodes Island employee. He's a project testing manager at Volvort Kochinski. He's a busy man, so it's only natural he hasn't had the time to leave Columbia and come visit.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Volvort Kochinski? Why did he send me to Rhodes Island, then?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I'm not too sure myself. You should probably ask him.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: He's the one you were the most proud of. I'm sure he'll be glad to tell you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Now don't be like that. I'm proud of all of you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: All of you, Hank.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: All of you...

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Ma'am, it's time. May I get you something?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hm? Booze time?

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Yes, ma'am. It's 9 o'clock.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hell yeah. Give me a 'Raging Sands.'

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And give this guy a 'Liberi Tears.'

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Instructor, I—

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Say no more. I get it.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Coming right up.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Instructor...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Come, tell me, how did you survive?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: If my memory serves, my objections didn't change anything, right...?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: The field commander sent us to the front lines. He treated us like cannon fodder.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Thankfully, his men didn't think that way.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: They saw us as a kind of symbol. They saw in us you.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: It was like as long as we were there, Sergeant Major Makayla Springthunder was there fighting the battle with them.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I was just a sergeant. Where'd they get the major part...?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: *Sigh*... And then?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: We finished our original objectives with the help of the surrounding units, and after getting some rest, they sent us a new mission.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: To seize the enemy's HQ.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: The enemy forces weren't in any shape to mount much resistance, so we split into two teams as soon as we reached their HQ.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: One team stayed outside, to mop up any remaining hostiles and provide support. The other went inside.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: We never thought the enemy would blow up their HQ to take everyone with them. The guys who went inside didn't make it out alive.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: This apparently drove a wedge between the top brass after the war was over, and while they were busy fighting each other, we were reassigned from the front.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: And a couple months after that, our team was discharged.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Just like you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Yeah, I know.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: All of us blamed ourselves. We were lost.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: We used to think that, as Columbian citizens, it was our duty to answer the president's call to join the military, to protect our homeland, to defend our borders and beliefs. That's what we were meant to do.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: But actually, all we did in the service was put up with a bunch of arrogant officers.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yelling at our teammates didn't do anything, and taking our anger out on you wasn't going to get us anywhere, but that one month, aside from our training and work, we were stuck in that cycle of negative emotion.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: After we were discharged, most of us went back to Columbia. It was only once I adjusted back to civilian life that those negative emotions started to fade away.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I don't know much about strategy, but if it wasn't for you, that war would not have ended so quickly.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: That victory was Columbia's, but if it wasn't for your decisive assault putting pressure on the commanders, the tug-of-war that came afterwards would've been far worse, and more men would've died on the field.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: How come you're so good at comforting people, but you're terrible at making conversation, Hank?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Please stop making fun of me, Instructor...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Oh, don't mind me too much. It's just something I said off the top of my head.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Right, weren't you going to take over the family business and rake in the dough? What happened to that? Why are you here at Rhodes Island, serving as an operator?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Report, Instructor—

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: No reporting. Just tell me like normal...

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I talked to my sister about it, and we decided that it was the best to have her take over the family business while I would be her second-in-command.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I thought you said you didn't get along with your sister... or at least that's what I think you told me before.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: But after I was discharged, I put some thought into it. Then, for the first time, I had a good discussion with her.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: She's been smart ever since we were kids. She majored in business too. We figured she would be the better choice to expand the family business.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: And when my father finally decides to retire and hand the business down to her, I'll leave Rhodes Island and go back home to help out.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Right now... I guess I'm here to earn some experience.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I wanted to expand my horizons through the lens of Rhodes Island and also make some connections, both inside and outside Columbia.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: This is very important to my life in the future.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Mm-hmm.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I've been wondering, but what does your family do again?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: We're in asset management.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Not sure what that is.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: My family manages the Maylander Child Rights Protection Foundation's wealth.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Maylander... Child Rights Protection Foundation?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: It's an NGO working to improve life for Columbian children.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: So a charity?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: If it's at all possible, I would like you to—

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, it really sounds like you were born for this kind of business.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Be sure to really throw yourself into that work.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Don't make a fool of yourself. Got it?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Right, good.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: As long as you're living well, I'm happy.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Gives me something to boast about to my coworkers, haha.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Ma'am, sir, your drinks.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: (Lights up Dur-nar's drink with Originium Arts)

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Enjoy.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Finally.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Downs the whole thing in one shot)

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Phew—Hot hot hot!

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Ah, that's the stuff.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: You're basically spitting fire, Instructor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Easy peasy.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You drink yours too.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Instructor, you know I—

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Drink it, Private Hank.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: That's an order.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor!

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: (Downs the beverage in one go)

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Huff—Phew...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: How is it?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: It's not that spicy, Instructor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, of course.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: That's just white grape juice.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: White grape juice?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, I can tell you don't go to bars often.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: 'Liberi Tears' is bartender lingo. It means a glass of white grape juice.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You think I forgot how allergic to alcohol you were?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Instructor...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You know how exhausting it was to carry you from the base to the army hospital that night? I'd rather not try that again.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Dario!

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Something else for you, ma'am?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: An 'Iceflame.'

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You, Hank? Another glass of Tears?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Just a moment.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Instructor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: What's up?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Where did you go after that court-martial?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well... I'd rather keep it to myself.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: I would like to know, please.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: And I'm sure the others would like to know as well.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: (Takes out a voice recorder)

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Uhh...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hold on, easy. Why the recorder?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: 'We' would like to know, Instructor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Oh, you prick. So this is why you came all the way here, why you're drinking with me?!

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: This is what all seventeen of us want to know.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: And I'm the only one who works at Rhodes Island, so it falls on me to do this.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And you couldn't have found somewhere more private...?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: It's easier to get you to talk in this environment.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: If we talked somewhere else, like the training grounds, you would definitely slip away with some work excuse.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: And I certainly wouldn't have been able to stop you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, you did your homework...

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: All thanks to you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: F-Fine, I'll go into it a little bit.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And I'll say this first: I don't remember everything. If I don't have an answer, pushing it isn't going to help.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Thanks, Instructor.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Here are your drinks.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Enjoy.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Just in time.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Let's talk and drink.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Takes a sip of the 'Iceflame')

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hah—That time—I think I went home right after they threw me out of the army.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I drowned my sorrows at the bars back home, day in and day out, then I'd go outside to make trouble.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: My family was understanding, at least. Pampered me all the time. They helped me keep from ending up a total failure.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: After that, my sister pulled some strings, and I got a job working riot police at the local department.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: What? These days, lots of little sisters outdo their big sisters, you know?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: She's much more mature than me. She always took care of everything back home when we were kids, too.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: It's like I should've been the little sister instead.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Takes a sip of the 'Iceflame')

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: It's a peaceful little town, so there wasn't much for me to do.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: After that, the city government decided to reorganize the police force and cut down on the riot police, so I got canned.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I guess they figured they could spend the money elsewhere, with how peaceful the place was.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: So I became a shut-in again and mooched off my parents. I felt bad about it, so I took some of the money I saved up and moved to a nearby nomadic city to look for work.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I looked around for a few weeks, and a company wanted me to help manage their security detail. I signed up without thinking too much about it.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: It wasn't until after I started that I found out their so-called security detail was just a few random bums they picked off the street to guard the place. They didn't have any training, and no equipment either.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I wanted to do something about it, but whenever I asked for a budget, the higher-ups would start making up excuses and told me not to worry about it if I knew what's good for me.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Now what's that about?!

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Seriously, bunch of douchebags!

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Takes a gulp of the 'Iceflame')

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I had nothing to say to those stupid suits and their fancy business, those jackwads!

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Well, it so happens that there was a convoy heading out to resupply pioneers hiring bodyguards.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: So I took a few of the kids who were willing to come with me and joined them as mercenaries.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Is that why when we first contacted your parents—

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You see, out in the frontier, it's not all that uncommon for a letter to take a whole month to not even get delivered.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Have you been out there?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You should see it for yourself, if you ever find the time.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I never thought I'd get to see places like that in Columbia.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: The food was terrible, and so was everything we had to use, but everyone held out hope for a good life.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: But then? Bandits, wild beasts, Catastrophes, you name it. You'll find them out there.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Those days were intense.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Rusthammers, beasts, gangs.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And the goddamned scouts.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: New Manfist's a helluva shithole.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Finishes the 'Iceflame')

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: *Cough*

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: None of the folks I brought with me made it out alive.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: It was just me, a disgraced old vet, cast out by the explorers, with nowhere to go except back to the city.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I went back home to find my old man had kicked the bucket. My little sister took over his work, while her big sister was as much a failure as she'd always been.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Heh...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Really, when I got the letter, I was wondering if a schlub like me really deserved an invite to this place.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And clearly I didn't need to worry about that.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Thanks to all of you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And you too, Corporal Mark Green.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I'm proud of all of you.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: (Turns off the recorder)

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: That's all I have to say.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Let's leave it there.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: Yes, Instructor.

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: (Puts his recorder away)

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Life here isn't bad. There's a bunch of cute kids to teach, a bunch of loyal, dependable coworkers to talk to, even a commander with a pretty good head.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Plus, I met an old friend here.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Not you. A Vulpo.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: She's an Infected girl. I fought her before with my electric blade. These days, though? We hang out and talk to each other.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: It's nice.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Makes me wonder how long this is going to last...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Dario!

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Yes, ma'am?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Any special cocktails you got in you? I'll take one.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You, Hank?

steps.name: Hank
steps.text: 'Liberi Tears,' thanks.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Heh, okay.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: There you go, Dario. His drinks are on me.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And bring some snacks.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: I gotta talk to my student some more.

steps.name: Dario
steps.text: Understood. Just a moment, please.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Alright, punk, the night is still young.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: We're drinking till we drop!
